AC1 — PER-DIRECTORY TRIAGE VERDICT (re-run fresh at 2026-08-12 18:15:04 PDT, immediately after claim)

Five guards per directory: (1) empty; (2) uncommitted; (3) `rebar exists` exits 1 (no such
ticket); (4) zero open file handles under it (`lsof +D`); (5) mtime older than 30 minutes.

    id                    empty  committed  exists  age_min  open_handles  VERDICT
    0efe-9207-2706-43a3   yes    no         no       322     0             DEBRIS - remove
    2021-2ef0-e36f-44fc   yes    no         no      1095     0             DEBRIS - remove
    6f8a-45e5-d9ec-402c   yes    no         no      1094     0             DEBRIS - remove
    a109-e758-71bb-4371   yes    no         no      1103     0             DEBRIS - remove
    afe5-db0b-e9c5-45d8   yes    no         no      3309     0             DEBRIS - remove
    c827-81ee-a592-4d27   yes    no         no      1097     0             DEBRIS - remove
    d052-ad3f-23c1-4511   yes    no         no      1125     0             DEBRIS - remove
    fa38-670c-d8fc-4c22   yes    no         no      1099     0             DEBRIS - remove

All 8 pass all five guards. NONE is excluded. The youngest (0efe, 5h22m) is an order of
magnitude outside the 30-minute live-writer window, so no directory is plausibly a live
agent's mid-write state — the specific confusion this triage exists to rule out.

Corroborating evidence, independent of the guards above:

* The tracker's `git status --porcelain` is EMPTY (0 lines) even with all 8 present — the
  expected signature, since git cannot track empty directories. That is also why these are
  invisible in shared history and exist only in this clone.
* `rebar review-plan` emitted, unprompted, one warning per directory:
  "skipping ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event: <path> (debris of an
  interrupted write; safe to delete)" — rebar's own classifier agrees with this verdict for
  all 8, by name.
* The live-writer control: `lsof +D` on the tracker DOES show an active handle on an
  unrelated ticket (`874a-bda3-ee6f-45eb/...-SNAPSHOT.json`), confirming the check can
  actually observe a concurrent writer and is not vacuously returning zero.

Mechanism: `os.makedirs(ticket_dir)` succeeded and the process died before the first event
was atomically renamed in — agents interrupted by host sleeps, session-limit kills, and
shell-cap timeouts. The mtime clustering supports this: six of the eight fall inside a
95-minute band on 2026-08-11 (23:30-00:01), consistent with a single interruption episode.

Tracker HEAD at triage: f79a163d70895b0119e652a9c71380b0df8f4799

comments.body:
AC2/AC3/AC4 — SWEEP EXECUTED AND VERIFIED (2026-08-13 01:16:16Z)

AC2 — run-level equality gate held. `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` re-run immediately
before any write reported `unpushed ticket commits: 0`, `stranded index entries: 0`, and a
`foreign top-level paths` list of exactly 8, byte-equal to the 8 triaged ids (sorted compare,
no diff). Because `--clean` is all-or-nothing over that set (it iterates the whole foreign
list and `shutil.rmtree`s each, with no per-directory filter), this equality assertion is the
only way to bound what it deletes — and it held, so no 9th path was in scope.

A NOTE ON A FIRST, ABORTED ATTEMPT: an earlier invocation of this same gate ABORTED with zero
writes. The cause was environmental, not a real mismatch — `rebar` was invoked with the
tracker worktree itself as cwd, which fails store attachment ("'tickets' is already used by
worktree"), so `--status` returned an error instead of a list and the equality check correctly
refused to proceed. Re-run from the throwaway checkout it passed. Recorded because the
fail-closed behaviour is the desired one: a gate that cannot read the current state must not
authorize a delete.

AC3 — removal succeeded. `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` reported
`repaired: 0 stranded, 8 foreign path(s) removed`.
  backup ref : refs/rebar-maintenance/20260813T011616Z
  rollback   : git reset --hard refs/rebar-maintenance/20260813T011616Z
  audit      : .tickets-tracker/.git/rebar-maintenance-audit.jsonl
The break-glass `--force` was NOT used and was not needed (0 unpushed ticket commits).
All 8 directories are confirmed absent from the filesystem.

BEFORE / AFTER fsck:
    before : 16 issues = 8 MISSING_CREATE + 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED + 1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH
                         + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH
    after  :  7 issues = 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH
    delta  : -8 MISSING_CREATE, -1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH; nothing else changed
`rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` returns 0.

The 7 remaining findings are the two classes deliberately left alone: STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED
(benign, already auto-resolved by the reducer) and ENV_ID_MISMATCH (known by-design flag from
change 1638). Neither was touched.

AC4 — no committed data modified. Tracker HEAD captured immediately before and immediately
after `--clean`, with no intervening ticket write:
    HEAD before : cc783205d744f426011ccdafb0a4a14cd16831df
    HEAD after  : cc783205d744f426011ccdafb0a4a14cd16831df   (identical)
`git status --porcelain` on the tracker: 0 lines, before and after. This is the expected
result and the reason the operation is safe — the removed directories were empty and
uncommitted, so git had nothing to track and no commit could reference them. Nothing was
removed from history; only untracked working-tree residue was cleared.

(HEAD does advance across the ticket's own event writes — create/claim/comment/close all
auto-commit. The assertion above is deliberately scoped to the `--clean` call itself, which is
what AC4 is about: the sweep must not alter committed ticket data.)

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`rebar fsck` reports 8 stray top-level directories in the tickets tracker
(`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`), each flagged twice — once as
`MISSING_CREATE` (no CREATE event found) and once inside the single
`FOREIGN_STORE_PATH` finding:

    0efe-9207-2706-43a3  2021-2ef0-e36f-44fc  6f8a-45e5-d9ec-402c  a109-e758-71bb-4371
    afe5-db0b-e9c5-45d8  c827-81ee-a592-4d27  d052-ad3f-23c1-4511  fa38-670c-d8fc-4c22

Baseline: `fsck complete: 16 issues found` = 8 MISSING_CREATE + 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED
+ 1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH.

## Evidence (pre-removal triage)

All 8 are empty directories (`ls -A` returns nothing), none is committed
(`git ls-tree HEAD <dir>` empty for all 8), `git status --porcelain` in the tracker is
clean because git cannot track empty directories, and `rebar exists <id>` returns exit 1
for all 8. `lsof +D` on the tracker shows no process holding a file under any of the 8.
Directory mtimes span 2026-08-10 11:05 to 2026-08-12 12:52 — all far outside the
~30-minute live-writer window (triage run 2026-08-12 17:59 PDT).
`rebar tracker-maintenance --status` independently reports `unpushed ticket commits: 0`
and exactly these 8 as `foreign top-level paths`, so `--clean` will not refuse and the
break-glass `--force` is NOT needed. `rebar review-plan` itself logs each one as
"debris of an interrupted write; safe to delete".

## Likely cause

`os.makedirs(ticket_dir)` succeeded and the process died before the first event was
atomically renamed in — agents interrupted mid-write by host sleeps, session-limit kills,
and shell-cap timeouts across the active fleet.

## How `--clean` actually behaves (correcting an earlier draft of this plan)

`rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` is ALL-OR-NOTHING over the foreign set:
`src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py` iterates `for name in foreign:` and calls
`shutil.rmtree(full)` on every entry that `fsck.foreign_store_path_list` returned, with no
per-directory filter and no CLI surface for passing a subset. The guards below therefore
do NOT select what the tool deletes — they are a precondition on running it at all.
Consequently the guard set is applied as an equality check: immediately before the write,
`--status`'s foreign list must be exactly the 8 triaged ids. If it lists any 9th path, or
any triaged directory has become non-empty, the run is ABORTED and reported rather than
narrowed — because there is no way to narrow it. This also bounds the check-then-act
(TOCTOU) window to the gap between that `--status` and the `--clean`, seconds apart.

## Relationship to 043f-3336-d5de-45be (closed)

That bug made the plan-relation reducer TOLERATE event-less directories and explicitly
rejected writer-side cleanup, because an automatic rmdir races a concurrent session's
in-flight write ("tolerate, never tidy"). This ticket does not reintroduce automatic
cleanup: it is a one-off operator-initiated sweep whose guards are precisely the evidence
an automatic writer-side rmdir could never establish.

## Plan (minimal, deterministic — five guards, all-or-nothing)

Per directory: (1) empty; (2) uncommitted; (3) `rebar exists <id>` exits 1; (4) no open
file handle under it; (5) mtime older than 30 minutes. Then the run-level gate: `--status`
foreign list equals the 8 triaged ids exactly. All six conditions hold -> run
`rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` (backup ref before first write, refusal on unpushed
ticket commits, durable audit). Any condition fails -> make NO writes and report back.
No raw git in the tracker, no stash. `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` (benign, auto-resolved) and
`ENV_ID_MISMATCH` (known by-design flag from change 1638) are out of scope and must not
be touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: A per-directory triage verdict for all 8 directories is recorded as a comment on
      this ticket, each citing the five guards. Verified by `rebar show 7c6e-4b8a-59c5-46db`
      showing a comment naming all 8 ids with a verdict each.
- [x] AC2: Immediately before any write, `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` is re-run and
      its `foreign top-level paths` list is asserted byte-equal to the 8 triaged ids;
      on any mismatch the sweep is aborted with no writes and the mismatch recorded.
      Verified by the recorded `--status` output in a ticket comment.
- [x] AC3: Given AC2's equality assertion held, `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` is run
      and exits 0 having printed a backup ref, and afterwards
      `rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` prints 0.
      If AC2's assertion failed instead, this criterion is satisfied by recording the abort
      and making no writes.
- [x] AC4: No committed ticket data is modified. Verified by capturing
      `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` before and after and asserting the two are
      byte-identical, and by `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` staying empty.

## Testing

A store data operation, so verification is by command exit code and before/after diff
rather than by unit test:

1. Before: `rebar fsck 2>&1 | tail -1` (record issue count);
   `git -C /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` (record sha).
2. Per-directory guards: `ls -A <dir>` empty; `git ls-tree HEAD <dir>` empty;
   `rebar exists <id>` exit 1; `lsof +D` naming no file under it; mtime > 30 min old.
3. Run-level gate: `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` foreign list == the 8 ids exactly.
4. Act: `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` — must exit 0 and print a backup ref.
5. After: `rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` must print 0;
   `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` must equal the step-1 sha;
   `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` must be empty.
